NimbusMart is a 2-year-old online retailer selling across Electronics, Home & Kitchen, Fashion, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors, and Books & Media. We grew steadily through 2024 and into early 2025 — but starting around Q3 2025, revenue has clearly softened, and even our Nov-Dec 2025 holiday season came in below last year's, which has never happened before.

We've tried throwing more discounts at the problem, but it doesn't seem to be working — margins are getting worse without a real sales recovery. My leadership team has a few theories (competitor activity in some regions, slower delivery, ad spend not converting like it used to, product quality issues) but no one has actually looked at the data.

Attached is our raw order-level transaction data for the last 2 years (~100,000 orders). Can you dig in and tell us:

  1. What's actually driving the decline — is it fewer customers, fewer orders per customer, lower basket size, or something else?
  2. Which regions, categories, channels, or marketing sources are underperforming, and is that difference statistically real or just noise?
  3. Are we losing our best customers, or is this a broad-based problem?
  4. What would you recommend we do about it — and how big could that fix be?

We need this to go beyond "here's a dashboard" — we want to know the why and the so what.

Data Dictionary¶

Column Description
order_id Unique order identifier
order_date Date of purchase (YYYY-MM-DD)
customer_id Unique customer identifier
customer_signup_date When the customer first registered
customer_region North / South / East / West / Central
customer_gender Male / Female / Other
customer_age Customer age
marketing_source Acquisition channel: Organic Search, Paid Ads, Referral, Email, Social Media
loyalty_tier Internal behavioral tier: Low / Medium / High (proxy for purchase frequency propensity)
product_id SKU identifier
category Electronics, Home & Kitchen, Fashion, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors, Books & Media
subcategory Sub-category within the category
unit_price Price per unit ($)
quantity Units purchased in this order line
discount_pct Discount applied (%)
total_amount Final amount paid ($), after discount
channel Website / Mobile App / Marketplace
payment_method Payment method used
delivery_days Days taken to deliver
return_flag 1 if the order was returned, else 0
customer_rating Post-purchase rating (1–5)

(Note: I did not tell you where the problem lives. Some patterns are subtle and some regions/categories/segments are red herrings — that's intentional, and it's exactly what makes this a realistic exercise rather than a lookup exercise.)

Problem Statement : The Revenue of NimbusMart is declining since the Q3 2025 and the Q4 2025 revenue was also less than Q4 2024 revenue.¶

Problem-Solving :¶

In an Ecommerce Business, Revenue is drived by the No of Active Customers, Avg number of orders per customer, Avg amount of order per each customer.

Revenue = No of Active Customer x avg number of orders per customer x avg amount of order per each customer.

Lets investigate each factor:

  1. No of Active Customer:

What is an active Customer ? As the data is about quarters, we assume an active customer is a customer who makes at least one purchase in each quarter, that is about 4 orders per annum.

No of Active Customers = Avg No of new customers acquired + (No of active customers in previous quarter * Avg Customer Retention Rate)

Now for any stable business, the rate of retention is about 30%. And Lets assume that the number of new customers being acquired are 1000 per month that is about 3000 per quarter.

So the customer base roughly becomes like:

no of active customers in Q1 2024 = 3000 + ( 0 * 0.3 ) = 3000
no of active customers in Q2 2024 = 3000 + ( 3000 * 0.3 ) = 3900
no of active customers in Q3 2024 = 3000 + ( 3900 * 0.3 ) = 4170
no of active customers in Q4 2024 = 3000 + ( 4170 * 0.3 ) = 4250
no of active customers in Q1 2025 = 3000 + ( 4250 * 0.3 ) = 4275
no of active customers in Q2 2025 = 3000 + ( 4275 * 0.3 ) = 4282
no of active customers in Q3 2025 = 3000 + ( 4282 * 0.3 ) = 4284
no of active customers in Q4 2025 = 3000 + ( 4284 * 0.3 ) = 4285
  • We see that after Q2 in 2025, the customer base became almost static. Apparently this was the time when the business revenue went downward.

  1. Avg Number of orders was considered to be 4 annually.

  2. Now Avg Amount of order per each customer.

  • This number has to be assumed.
  • Lets say an avg order will have 1 basic electronic (~1200 - ~2500), 2 Home and kitchen(~800 - ~1400), 4 Fashion Elements(~2000 - ~4000), 1 Sports and outdoor(~1000 - ~1400), and 1 book(~200).
  • So, an estimated total can be ~5200 - ~9500 Rupees.

So Revenue in the Q3 Must be around : 8.9Cr - 16.2Cr

So if the Revenue Dopped in the third Quarter of 2025, Either or a combination of the drivers faced a decrease in number. Lets find that out using data.

import pandas as pd

# Step 1: Build quarter identifiers for signup and orders
df["signup_qid"] = df["signup_year"].astype(str) + "Q" + df["signup_quarter"].astype(str)

df["order_year"] = pd.to_datetime(df["order_date"]).dt.year
df["order_quarter"] = pd.to_datetime(df["order_date"]).dt.quarter
df["order_qid"] = df["order_year"].astype(str) + "Q" + df["order_quarter"].astype(str)

# Step 2: Get new customers per signup quarter
cohorts = df.groupby("signup_qid")["customer_id"].unique()

# Step 3: Get active customers per order quarter
active = df.groupby("order_qid")["customer_id"].unique()

# Step 4: Compute retention
retention_rates = []
quarters = sorted(cohorts.index)

for i in range(len(quarters)-1):
    curr_q = quarters[i]
    next_q = quarters[i+1]

    new_custs = set(cohorts[curr_q])
    next_active = set(active[next_q])

    overlap = len(new_custs.intersection(next_active))
    retention_rate = round((overlap / len(new_custs) if len(new_custs) > 0 else 0)*100)

    retention_rates.append({
        "signup_quarter": curr_q,
        "retention_rate_%": retention_rate
    })

retention_df = pd.DataFrame(retention_rates)

retention_df

In the quarter 3 the number of orders increased but the average order value (AOV) of the quarter decreased. So this can be a factor of decline in the revenue. We will investigate this as well.¶

Now We will state our hypothesis:¶

  1. Average Order Value dropped dramatically in the Q3 of 2025.
  2. Customer Acquisition has steadily declined.

We will look at each of them one by one.¶

Q4. What is the change in discount that was being given to the customers ?¶

In [56]:
q3_2024_discount = round(q3_2024_data['discount_pct'].mean(),2)

print(f"The Average discount % given on the orders in Q3 of 2024 was: {q3_2024_discount}")

The Average discount % given on the orders in Q3 of 2024 was: 6.05
In [57]:
q3_2025_discount = round(q3_2025_data['discount_pct'].mean(),2)

print(f"The Average discount % given on the orders in Q3 of 2024 was: {q3_2025_discount}")

The Average discount % given on the orders in Q3 of 2024 was: 22.03

We Found the culprit here. The average discount percentage that was being given to customers in quarter 3 of 2025 was 22% which is about 16% more than the average discount percentage that was given in quarter 3 of 2024. This is the reason the revenue dropped significantly even when the number of orders increased.¶

Insight:¶

NimbusMart adopted a broad-based discount strategy in Q3 2025. However, the increase in discounts did not generate proportional growth in order volume or customer acquisition. Instead, it coincided with a decline in Average Order Value and overall revenue, suggesting the strategy eroded revenue more than it stimulated demand.

II. Customer Acquisition dropped significantly.¶

Now instead of formulating questions here. Lets find out using the data.¶

From the data we can understand that there is no significant evidence to believe that one loyalty tier customers performed worse than the other as all of the tier customers gradually increased in no of orders.¶
So There is no specific need to implement a segment wise strategy in this segment.¶

Marketing Source¶

  • We already realized that all of the marketing sources' performance decreased gradually with time. So we need to implement some strategies for all the sources so that the new customers who are subjected to different marketing sources signup in bigger numbers.
  • The marketing team must evaluate and analyze the performances of the different marketing sources and understand the point where things are going downward.

Hypothesis Testing: We will be testing our hypothesis.¶

The discount percentage in q3 2025 was 16% more than q3 2024.**

H0 : The mean discount percentage of Q3 2024 was less than or equal to mean discount percentage of Q3 2025

Ha : The mean discount percentage of Q3 2025 was more than the mean discount percentage of Q3 2024.

In [101]:
# Now this is going to be right tail test

# We are compairing two different independent samples here so we will use the t-test of independence for this.

from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

discount_pct_2024Q3 = df[df['order_qid'] == "2024Q3"]['discount_pct']
discount_pct_2025Q3 = df[df['order_qid'] == "2025Q3"]['discount_pct']

t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(discount_pct_2024Q3, discount_pct_2025Q3)

alpha = 0.05

if p_value < alpha :
  print(f"The p-value is less than alpha: {p_value}. We reject the Null Hypothesis.")
else:
  print(f"The p-value is more than alpha: {p_value}. We fail to reject the Null hypothesis.")

The p-value is less than alpha: 0.0. We reject the Null Hypothesis.
  • There is enough evidence to conclude that the discount percentage in Q3 2025 was significantly higher than the discount percentage in Q3 2025.

Insights :¶

  1. No of New Customers being acquired dropped significantly starting in the beginning of this year and accelerated in the end of the year.
  2. Even when the revenue decreased since the start of 2025, the number of orders actually increased which demonstrates that the old customers are still actively making order purchases.
  3. The retention rate was actually stable throughout the business lifetime.
  4. Average Order Value (AOV) decreased drastically in the third quarter of 2025.
  5. The product categories that were being ordered in the Q3 of Year1 were consistent even in Q3 of Year2.
  6. The average number of items in an order placed in Q3 2024 are 2 which is same as Q3 2025.
  7. And the average unit price in Q3 2024 is about 66 Rupees which is also exactly similar to Q3 of 2025.
  8. The Average discount % in Q3 2024 was about 6-6.5%, but the same in Q3 2025 was pushed all the way upto 22-22.5% which is 16% increment. This is serious and this was the factor that most strongly associated with the decrease of the overall revenue.
  9. Now the discount was made universally and not specific to a category and this strategy turned out to be ineffective in terms of no of orders placed.
  10. When we inspected the segment-wise performance, we realized that each of the metric and segment actually performed better this year compared to same period in the last year.
  • So the main two elements which contributed to overall decrement of the revenue were:
    1. The Universal discount given in an attempt to increase number of orders.
    2. Customer Acquisition failing gradually.

Recommendations:¶

  1. The marketing sources which are responsible for bringing in new customers is to be inspected and review for their performance and the point where the things are getting bad must be determind.
  2. The discount approach must be converted from universal approach on each order to segment wise approch like:
  • Giving more benefits to high value customers.
  • Giving considerable discount to customers who are at risk to leave.
  • Giving Discounts only on product categories which are moving considerably slow compared to others.

Since this notebook is intended as a Data Analyst portfolio project, I'd include three hypothesis tests:

✅ Independent t-test → Average Order Value ✅ Independent t-test → Discount Percentage ✅ Chi-square Test → Product Category Distribution

Future Procedures:¶

Post application of the recommendation we can test the strength of recommendation and their impacts by:

  1. Constantly monitoring the KPIs for the business.
  2. Perform A/B Testing on the customers and find out whether the strategies were good enough.
  3. Understand what factors have more potential to increase the business.
  4. We can perform customers segmentation analysis to analyze, were there any changes in the performances.
  5. Perform Root Cause analysis again and understand if the problem that we were facing actually fade off.
